title: Bridgelet mini-bootpack: runloop playflow & bootcamp notes
body:
TL;DR
A compact, instructor-friendly runbook for a 45–90 minute Bridgelet mini-bootpack: a hands-on, low-friction workshop that takes an engineer from 'unfamiliar' to 'can ship a small integration' using the SDK. Focus areas: minimal environment setup, runloop (request->observe->iterate), quick telemetry checks, and survival checklist for common failure modes.

Audience
- New integrators (backend/frontend engineers) who need a short, repeatable onboarding to embed Redwood SDK features.
- Internal developer advocates running 1:many office hours and quick demos.

Goals
1) Ship a tiny demo that calls the SDK (chat or completion) end-to-end.
2) Demonstrate runloop checkpoints: local dev, sandbox, telemetry, and basic gating.
3) Surface three common failure modes and mitigation patterns.
4) Produce a small checklist the integrator can reuse after the session.

Timebox and formats
- 45 minute quickloop: local-only, no network dependencies beyond Redwood hosted API.
- 75–90 minute bootcamp: includes canary routing exercise, telemetry validation, and simple rollouts.
- Formats: remote pairing (screen share), in-person 5–8 people lab, or async self-serve with walkthrough notes.

Prerequisites (attendee)
- GitHub account, basic terminal familiarity.
- Node 18+ or Python 3.10+ installed.
- Redwood trial API key (or local SDK stub).
- Optional: Docker for sandboxing.

Instructor prep checklist
- Confirm API key with correct scopes.
- Provision a shared sample project repo (link below).
- Start a sandbox server or provide a local mock (script in repo: scripts/run-local-mock.sh).
- Pre-seed telemetry dashboard with a fake request so attendees see the shape.
- Print the failure-mode cards (quick slips) or have them as slides.

Playflow: step-by-step runloop
1) 0–10m: context & TL;DR demo
   - Quick live demo that shows a single request and result (keep it under 90s).
   - Emphasize: what success looks like (token cost, latency, stable output).

2) 10–25m: local-first setup
   - Clone repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood/bridgelet-bootpack.git
   - Install: pnpm install (or pip install -r requirements.txt)
   - Add API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_trial_xxx (or set env in .env)
   - Quick smoke: node examples/simple-chat.js (or python examples/simple_chat.py)
   - Expected: single JSON response containing assistant message, ~2s local runtime.

3) 25–45m: instrument + iterate
   - Add metadata: attach request_id and feature flags to a sample call.
   - Show batching toggle: local config file (config/runloop.json) with batch_size 1 -> 8.
   - Demonstrate impact on latency and token cost using the included bench script: scripts/bench.sh --n=50 --batch=8
   - Observe telemetry: open /console/routes/demo-chat and show per-token breakdown.

4) 45–65m: sandbox canary (if time)
   - Flip a route to canary a quantized model variant: route config snippet
       route: /generate-demo
       model: x-small-quant-v2
       fallback: gpt-like-stable
       rollout: 10% canary
   - Trigger traffic using scripts/traffic-gen.sh --duration 60s
   - Inspect traces: latency distribution, error spikes, and fallback counts.

5) 65–90m: failure drills and recovery
   - Simulate KV-cache miss / warmup cost: cold start spike and mitigation (explicit warmup call).
   - Inject elevated token length requests to trigger autoscaling: watch dedicated pool metrics.
   - Network flakiness: demonstrate local retry policy and fallback to cached prefix.

Failure modes (cards) + mitigations
- Failure: Missing API scopes -> Symptom: 401 or truncated responses.
  Mitigation: pre-check script that validates token scopes and prints a human-friendly error. (scripts/check-key.sh)
- Failure: Sudden latency spike on quantized variant -> Symptom: 95th p latency jump.
  Mitigation: Canary routing with instant fallback to a higher latency but more reliable variant.
- Failure: Telemetry absent or mismatched -> Symptom: dashboard shows zero events.
  Mitigation: lightweight test harness that emits a known marker event and asserts ingestion within N seconds.

Telemetry & success gating (mini-SLOs)
- Per-route SLOs to show in console: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 750ms, error rate < 1%.
- Telemetry sanity checks run at end of lab: scripts/telemetry-check.sh --route demo-chat
- Recommended minimal fields to emit with each request: request_id, team, feature_flag, model_tag, sample_prompt_hash.

Pocket scripts and commands (copy-friendly)
- Smoke test (node):
    node examples/simple-chat.js
- Bench (bash):
    scripts/bench.sh --n=100 --batch=4
- Local mock (start):
    ./scripts/run-local-mock.sh
- Canary flip (example curl):
    curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      https://console.redwood.ai/api/routes/update \
      -d '{"route":"/generate-demo","rollout":0.10,"model":"x-small-quant-v2"}'

Minimal example (Python snippet)
- purpose: show request + metadata attachment

    from redwood import RedwoodClient
    c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
    resp = c.chat.route('/generate-demo').send(
        messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Write a 2-line product blurb."}],
        metadata={"request_id":"lab-{{uuid}}","feature":"bridgelet-minilab"}
    )
    print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

Outputs to capture for grading (self-check)
- Was the sample request successful? (Y/N)
- Did telemetry register the request (assert marker seen)? (Y/N)
- Did the canary fallback occur under simulated stress? (Y/N or N/A)
- Were failure drill mitigations exercised? (Y/N)

Appendix: quick heuristics for instructors
- Keep the demo fast: pre-warn attendees where they might get stuck (env vars, Node version).
- Provide a 'skip-to' section in the README for those who only want telemetry/canary steps.
- Pair novices with an advocate for the first 15 minutes.

Notes to self / open questions (TODO)
- Add a tiny UI mock to demonstrate streaming partial responses (is there bandwidth?).
- Should we include a pre-run telemetry dataset for offline demos? (ask observability team)
- Confirm whether admin API tokens are allowed in public workshop repos; maybe switch to ephemeral tokens.

Related artifacts and links
- Workshop repo: https://github.com/redwood/bridgelet-bootpack
- Canary routing RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/bridgelet-routes
- Telemetry dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/demo-chat

Small immediate next steps (short checklist)
- [ ] Add 'skip-to' cheat links in README (Maya)
- [ ] Generate ephemeral API keys for upcoming public office hours (Ravi)
- [ ] Add telemetry-check script into repo and document expected output (Avery)

End of notes.
